Privacy

We do not ask for, collect or store personal information. This page lists everything that does happen when you visit.

The short version

  • No accounts, no sign-up, no advertising, no analytics and no tracking of any kind.
  • One cookie, hp_theme, remembers whether you chose the light or dark theme. Nothing else is stored on your device.
  • Your approximate location, worked out by our hosting provider from your connection, is used for that one page view to show hazards near you, and then discarded.
  • Every font, script and map on the site is served from hazardpulse.com. No third party is contacted while you browse.

Your approximate location

HazardPulse runs on Cloudflare’s network. For each page request, Cloudflare gives our code an estimate of where the request came from (latitude and longitude, city and country). We use it, during that request only, to mark your approximate position on our maps and to say how far you are from the nearest active hazard.

We never store it, log it or send it anywhere. The API and the data files never use it.

Cookies and local storage

NamePurposeValuesKept for
hp_themeRemembers your light or dark theme, set only when you press the theme button. The same value is also kept in your browser’s local storage.light or darkOne year (SameSite=Lax, Secure)

Delete it at any time in your browser settings; the site then follows your system theme.

Hosting

Like any website, requests pass through our hosting provider, Cloudflare, which processes connection data such as IP addresses to deliver the site and protect it from abuse, under its own privacy policy. The API limits each address to 120 requests a minute; that count is held in memory for a minute and never stored.

Where the hazard data comes from

Public data from government agencies and published science — the full list, model by model, is on the methods page. No personal or user-contributed data is used.
